title: Advanced While Loops
bullets: Keep asking until input is valid.
End a while loop with break.

title: Infinite Loops
paragraphs: An infinite loop never reaches an exit.
The condition in while True stays True. This example waits for input during every iteration.
Press Enter to complete an iteration. Use Stop to end this example.
A loop can also repeat endlessly when a value needed by its stopping condition is never updated.

title: Nesting while Loops
paragraphs: The inner loop runs inside the outer loop.
Set column back to 0 at the start of each row. This lets the inner loop run again.
Increase column inside the inner loop. Increase row after the inner loop finishes.
code:
row = 0
while row < 2:
    column = 0
    while column < 2:
        print(row, column)
        column += 1
    row += 1

title: Validating a Choice
paragraphs: Validation checks whether input meets the requirements.
Here, only yes and no are accepted. The loop repeats while the answer matches neither choice.
Any other response causes another prompt. The accepted value is displayed after the loop.
code:
answer = ""
while answer != "yes" and answer != "no":
    answer = input("Enter yes or no: ")
print("Accepted:", answer)
expectedOutput:
Enter yes or no: maybe
Enter yes or no: yes
Accepted: yes
initialOutput:
Enter yes or no: maybe
Enter yes or no: yes
Accepted: yes

title: Validating a Whole Number
paragraphs: The loop keeps asking while age is negative.
The try block attempts the conversion with int.
A ValueError means the text could not be converted. The except block displays a message.
The loop ends when age is 0 or higher.
expectedOutput:
Enter your age: -3
Enter your age: hello
Enter a whole number.
Enter your age: 17
Valid age: 17
initialOutput:
Enter your age: -3
Enter your age: hello
Enter a whole number.
Enter your age: 17
Valid age: 17

title: Validating Inputs Separately
paragraphs: Give each input its own validation loop.
The first loop accepts red or blue. The second accepts small or large.
An invalid size only repeats the size prompt. The accepted colour is kept.
code:
colour = ""
while colour != "red" and colour != "blue":
    colour = input("Colour (red/blue): ")
size = ""
while size != "small" and size != "large":
    size = input("Size (small/large): ")
print(colour, size)
expectedOutput:
Colour (red/blue): red
Size (small/large): medium
Size (small/large): small
red small
initialOutput:
Colour (red/blue): red
Size (small/large): medium
Size (small/large): small
red small

title: Ending a while Loop with break
paragraphs: while True keeps its condition True. A break can still end the loop.
Here, entering quit executes break. No later instruction in that iteration runs.
Python then runs the final print outside the loop.
expectedOutput:
Command: hello
Received: hello
Command: quit
Loop complete.
initialOutput:
Command: hello
Received: hello
Command: quit
Loop complete.

title: Skipping an Iteration with continue
paragraphs: continue skips the rest of the current iteration. The loop then checks its condition again.
Here, number increases before the continue check. The loop can still reach its stopping value.
The value 3 is skipped. The values 4 and 5 are displayed.
code:
number = 0
while number < 5:
    number += 1
    if number == 3:
        continue
    print(number)
print("Loop complete.")

title: break Inside Nested while Loops
paragraphs: A break ends the nearest loop that contains it.
Here, the inner loop ends when column reaches 1.
The outer loop still increases row. It then starts another inner loop.

title: Wrap Up
bullets: A loop needs a reachable exit to finish. Use Stop to interrupt an example that keeps running.
Reset inner-loop variables when each outer iteration begins.
Validation loops keep asking until input meets the requirements.
Use break to end the nearest containing loop.
Use continue to skip the rest of an iteration. Keep the stopping condition reachable.
